title: Training Notes — Crediting the Returned Payment Fee Against an Independent Living Late Fee
content:
On an Independent Living Residency Agreement account, the returned payment fee already charged for a returned payment is credited against the late fee.

**Rule.** Where exactly one returned payment was posted within the 12 months ending on the day of assessment and an ACH autopay payment was posted within the one month ending on that day, the late fee is reduced by the returned payment fee. Where exactly one returned payment was posted within those 12 months and no ACH autopay payment was posted within that month, the late fee is reduced by half of the returned payment fee, rounded to the cent half up. Otherwise the late fee is not reduced. The reduction is taken from the greater of the flat late fee and the percentage amount, and the late fee never goes below zero.

The returned payment fee is 35.00 for every apartment type (Studio, One-Bedroom, One-Bedroom Deluxe, Two-Bedroom, Two-Bedroom Deluxe and Cottage Home); half of it, rounded half up, is 17.50.

## Questions and answers

**Q. Which payments count as ACH autopay payments?**
A. Payment entries posted with the ACH autopay method within the one month ending on the day of assessment. A one-time ACH payment, a check or a card payment is not an ACH autopay payment.

**Q. What if two returned payments were posted within the 12 months?**
A. The late fee is not reduced; only exactly one returned payment gives a credit.

**Q. What if no payment was ever returned?**
A. The late fee is not reduced.

## Truth table

| Returned payments within the 12 months | ACH autopay payment within the one month | Reduction of the late fee |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly one | Yes | 35.00 |
| Exactly one | No | 17.50 |
| None | Either | None |
| Two or more | Either | None |

Hypothetical example: a greater amount of 75.72 with exactly one return in the year and an ACH autopay payment last week becomes 40.72.
